title: Chiang Mai Marathon 2026 Review: Tha Phae Gate to the King's Monument
seo_title: Chiang Mai Marathon 2026 Review | Muang Thai Race Guide
meta_description: The Muang Thai Chiang Mai Marathon 2026: December 20 starting at Tha Phae Gate, finishing at the King Naresuan Monument. Four distances from 3K to full marathon, registration open from THB 1,500 — reviewed.
dek: Set for 20 December 2026, this Jog & Joy-produced marathon starts at Chiang Mai's iconic Tha Phae Gate and finishes at the King Naresuan the Great Monument in Mae Rim. Four distances (42K, 21K, 10K, 3K), registration open from THB 1,500. Here's what to expect from one of northern Thailand's most established marathon productions.
verdict: The Muang Thai Chiang Mai Marathon is one of Thailand's premier road races — a Jog & Joy production with a point-to-point course that starts at the iconic Tha Phae Gate in Chiang Mai's old city and finishes at the King Naresuan the Great Monument in Mae Rim. That's a route with real narrative: old-city start, countryside middle, monument finish. Four distances from 3K to the full 42.195km make it genuinely inclusive, the December date is northern Thailand's coolest month, and — crucially — registration is open right now from THB 1,500. With a reliability score of 100, it's the most data-confident race on the 2027 calendar. Suits runners who want a northern Thai marathon with a scenic point-to-point course, a proven organiser, and cool-season conditions that rival anywhere in Southeast Asia.

sections.heading: The Course: Old City to Mountain Monument
paragraphs: The race starts at Tha Phae Gate — the eastern entrance to Chiang Mai's old city and the most photographed landmark in northern Thailand — and finishes at the King Naresuan the Great Monument in Mae Rim district, roughly 15km north of the city. [1] That point-to-point format gives the course a genuine sense of progression: you leave the old-city moat behind, pass through Chiang Mai's northern suburbs, and climb gently toward the Mae Rim valley with Doi Suthep mountain as your western backdrop.

sections.heading: The Organiser: Jog & Joy, Presented by Muang Thai
paragraphs: Jog & Joy Co., Ltd. is one of Thailand's most established race production companies, with a portfolio of northern Thai events and a reputation for professional timing, well-stocked aid stations, and smooth race-day logistics. [1] The Muang Thai insurance brand's presenting sponsorship adds commercial backing — expect quality medals, race tees, and a well-resourced finish festival. The entry fee starts at THB 1,500, which is competitive for a full marathon with this level of production.

sections.heading: The Distances: Four Options, Full Marathon as Headliner
paragraphs: Four distances are offered: a full marathon (42.195km), half marathon (21.1km), 10km, and 3km. [1] The 3km fun run opens the event to families and first-timers, while the full marathon's point-to-point course is the main event for serious runners. December in Chiang Mai is genuinely cool — morning temperatures in the low-to-mid teens Celsius, often with a light fog over the old city at flag-off. It's as good as marathon weather gets in Southeast Asia.

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: The Muang Thai Chiang Mai Marathon is one of the strongest picks on the entire Southeast Asian calendar: a point-to-point course from Tha Phae Gate to a mountain monument, a proven organiser, cool December conditions, and registration that's open right now at a competitive price point. If you're building a 2026/2027 calendar, this deserves a spot near the top. Register via chiangmaimarathon.com. The 2026 edition is set for 20 December. [1]
